response.query: Which plausible exogenous shocks in a hot Brazilian city centre (permit changes, municipal interventions, major weather events, festivals) are available and time-stamped enough to serve as instruments or natural experiments?
response.answer: Major weather events, like heatwaves or unusual rainfall, and municipal interventions, such as temporary permit changes, serve as plausible instruments or natural experiments in São Paulo. Festivals may also provide time-stamped exogenous shocks.

results.title: GSR 2025 | Global Overview
results.content: In 2024, global renewable energy growth was primarily driven by the power sector, where capacity expanded by 741 gigawatts (GW), the largest annual increase ever recorded. 3  Despite this momentum, renewable energy growth could not keep pace with rising global electricity demand. While some countries accelerated their investments in renewables and energy storage to reduce risk and increase resilience, fossil fuel investments also grew, often driven by industrial lobbying and short-term security concerns. Renewable-powered mini- and microgrids support adaptation to climate impacts and energy system shocks in both remote and urban settings, through technologies such as wind and solar power and geothermal energy. 15  Other renewable sources – whether for power, heat or transport fuels – accounted for only small additions to the global energy supply. :   A certificate awarded to certify the generation of one unit of renewable energy (typically 1 MWh of electricity but also less commonly of heat).
